title: N.C.R.B., (M.H.A.) CRIME IN INDIA - 1994 17.5.4 The above figures which include baggage seizures, demonstrate that there has been a fall in the smuggling of precious metals over the years since 1991. The quantity of gold smuggled in has also fallen from 5596 kgs in 1990 to 1147 kgs in 1994. Similar is the case with silver which recorded 220318 kgs in 1990 and dwindled to 6404 kgs in 1994. The goods such as synthetic fibres, diamonds also recorded a considerable fall. One contributing factor could be the liberalised import policy in the context of liberalisation of the economy adopted in the present decade. 'Narcotic Drugs' are, however, found to be in the priority list of smuggling in 1994 compared to the previous years. There has been a sharp increase of around 350 percent (from 15.8 crores in 1993 to 54.3 crores in 1994) in the value of the 'Drugs' seized by the customs. Electronic goods also seem to be much sought after items for smuggling in 1994 because of perceived premium and the value of the seized articles accounting to Rs. 37.2 crores compared to Rs.35.8 crores in 1993.
